teaching.en: Oak Street records 120 disposable cups every Friday. I propose a £900 refill station beside the bus stop. If the station is installed and clearly signed, cup use may fall because people can refill bottles. The measure is practical because it uses one visible location and a stated budget. Volunteers should count discarded cups for four Fridays before installation and four Fridays after it. This indicator will show whether the action changes the documented problem without promising that all cup waste will disappear.

answer.text: Oak Street records 120 disposable cups every Friday. I propose a £900 refill station beside the bus stop. If the station is installed and clearly signed, cup use may fall because people can refill bottles. The measure is practical because it uses one visible location and a stated budget. Volunteers should count discarded cups for four Fridays before installation and four Fridays after it. This indicator will show whether the action changes the documented problem without promising that all cup waste will disappear.

I propose installing a refill station beside the Oak Street bus stop for £900. The street currently records 120 disposable cups each Friday. If the station is installed and signs are added, residents may choose reusable bottles more often. The expected effect is a lower cup count, not the complete end of waste. Volunteers can measure progress by counting cups for four Fridays before and after installation. This practical indicator connects the local cause, the action and a limited result that the community can actually check.

feedback.es: The source supplies baseline, action, budget, condition, effect and follow-up.

answer.text: I propose installing a rainwater tank at Hill Garden before June. The tank costs £1,200, and the garden currently uses 4,000 litres of mains water per summer week. If rainwater is collected and used on plants, demand from the mains may decrease. Some mains water may still be needed. Staff can check the result by recording weekly litres for eight weeks and comparing them with the baseline. This measurable indicator links the action to a cautious effect without making an unsupported promise.

Hill Garden uses 4,000 litres of mains water each summer week. I propose a £1,200 rainwater tank for the garden. If the tank is installed before June, mains-water use may fall because stored rain can be used on plants. The proposal does not promise to remove all mains use. Staff should record litres used each week for eight weeks and compare the figure with the current 4,000-litre baseline. This indicator will show whether the practical measure produces the expected local effect.

feedback.es: The recovery uses a garden scenario with a measurable water indicator.
